title: AIP Kernel v0.1 — Message Schema
description: JSON Schema for the AIP (AI Interaction Protocol) Kernel v0.1 (SPEC.md). Validates the shared envelope and the four message types: event, action, result, error. Enforces: 4 message types only; no in_reply_to on events; no idempotency/risk overrides on actions; result MUST reference an action id; terminal result statuses; the 10 kernel error codes. The binding-level hello/ping/pong frames are NOT application messages and are intentionally not covered here.

v.description: Protocol version. Kernel v0.1 = 1. Anything else: UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.

type.description: Exactly these four. Anything else: INVALID_MESSAGE.

id.description: Message ID, unique within the (session, source) stream at minimum; SHOULD be a ULID/UUID. Resent messages keep their original id.

in_reply_to.description: ID of the message this message answers. MUST be absent on events (SPEC §5.3).

seq.description: Monotonically increasing within the (session, source) stream (SPEC §5.4, I7). No global sequence.

ts.description: Epoch milliseconds. Informational only; MUST NOT be used for ordering or timeouts (I8).

source.description: Participant identity, bound to an authenticated principal at transport level (I9).

name.description: Semantic event name (dot-namespaced). Business state change, never raw telemetry (SPEC §11.3).

data.description: Minimum state required to decide. For large state, send a reference instead (context profile, SPEC §9.2).

name.description: Named capability invocation, e.g. browser.click, erp.order.approve. The Kernel defines zero actions (SPEC §9.3).

target.description: Reference to an entity from an earlier event's data.

actionPayload.description: Actions MUST NOT carry idempotency or risk metadata; those are Registry/policy properties, never per-call parameters (SPEC §4.2, §9.3, §9.4).

event.description: Bare reference: the event the decision engine asserts should follow. Matching semantics are profile material (SPEC §9.8).

in_reply_to.description: MUST reference the action.id this result answers (SPEC §5.3).

status.description: accepted/running are non-terminal; ok/failed/timeout/rejected are terminal (SPEC §6.2).

code.description: Executor-defined failure code (lower-case, namespaced, e.g. target_not_found) for status=failed. MUST NOT collide with kernel error codes (SPEC §4.6).

duplicate.description: True when this result replays a previously settled action; MUST carry original_result_id (SPEC §6.3).

original_result_id.description: ID of the original terminal result when duplicate=true.

code.description: Kernel error registry, exhaustive (SPEC §4.6). Extension codes live in their own namespace (e.g. context.not_found) and are not part of this schema.

allowed.description: Retryability is declared by the sender of the error/result, never guessed by the receiver (SPEC §4.5, C.7).
